summary:
I did fixer B's items 5–8 in C:\Users\louis\Documents\RANDOM\ROBLOX\Blacksmithing Game. Nothing is committed and Studio was not touched. The final `lune run scripts/verify` is green on a quiet machine: 732 pass, 0 fail, VERIFY GREEN in 277.7 s, exit 0. The machine was 1 % busy at the start and 13 % at the end, with no other Lune process.

**Item 5: the physics frame uses kept parts only.**
- `MassProps.physicsFrame(parts, kept, gripSlot)` now takes the kept Grip parts. The vote's rules are unchanged, and no kept Grip part gives the origin and +Y, as no Grip part does today.
- V4 runs before the verdict, so it keeps every Grip part through a new `validationFrame`.
- I tried wider than the lead's item, as the lead asked. Two more places let a cleaned part steer the report, so I closed them with the same kept-parts rule (this is a deviation, see below):
  - **The guard line.** A Guard block hidden in F2's blade moved balance −0.057 → −0.131 and cutIndex 0.425 → 0.4065.
  - **The grip's top on a guardless sword.** A hidden Grip block took cutIndex 0.40 → 0.
- Now V2's strap hidden in A26's rings (turned 20° or 40°), A25, and those two blocks each measure exactly like the same design without the hidden part.
- **Bit-compare against m3-r1-base.** No design moves unless it cleans a Grip or Guard part.
  - Of the 136 fixtures, 15 move.
  - Of the 33,389 plausible designs, 1,785 move (676 with a cleaned Grip part, 1,109 with a cleaned Guard part); the full list is in `out/pl_moved.txt`.
  - Steps, edges, kept flags and owned volumes are bit-identical everywhere. cutIndex moves by at most 0.0043 on plausible designs and 0.0213 on fixtures.
- **Tests and goldens.**
  - Reference.spec now exempts and pins P1's guard line, the only prototype fixture that differs.
  - New case from hiddengrip.luau in MassProps.spec.
  - Goldens re-blessed: A25 now has F1's physics; P1 and its specks change balance and bladeLength. Digest fixtures group: 424,595 bytes, fnv1a32 2087286482.

**Item 6: §5's promise and §0.5.** Both now name three limits, each with its O-number: O9, O10 and O11. The promise carries the [Decision to confirm] marks.

**Item 7: the verifiers' tests.**
- T-DIF-02: §5.1's formula, plus a planted material term.
- T-DIF-07 (c): random grip stacks of 3–6 Blocks with more shuffles.
- Per-loop charges pinned by function name on F5, F4 and P5.
- §4.6's boundaries, and rangeOf's error path.
- All 23 mutants fail their test, and every filter passes on the tree.

**Item 8: the text.**
- V2's and V1's minors. The hidden-gap SurfaceComplexity channel, re-measured, is now under O10.
- O11 gives each fix's cost. The lattice Douglas–Peucker was re-tried on this tree: it moves no F, C, X or A value.
- The in-suite stretch figures, and that T-PERF-01 needs a quiet machine.
- T-PERF-01 run alone on this tree: slowest valid design 53.3–53.4 ms, about 139 ms Studio.
- `--quick` went from 29.20 s to 25.87 s: the fast generated-design corpora became t.slow, and T-DIF-07 (a)'s fast case was narrowed to C10 and C11.
- I corrected the re-cut maximum from 0.0378 to 0.0379. Fixer A's figure was measured before its raster fix.

deviations: Item 5 went wider than the lead's frame point and vote. The guard line (kept Guard parts) and the grip's top on a guardless sword (kept Grip parts) follow the same rule, because a cleaned Guard or Grip part steered bladeLength, cutIndex and the balance through them (measured). As a result, designs with a cleaned Guard part move too: 1,109 plausible designs, P1 and its specks, and worst valid 4, 5, 10 and 11. The lead expected only cleaned-Grip designs to move
V4 keeps every Grip part (new MassProps.validationFrame). It runs before the verdict alongside V1–V3; moving it after the verdict would change validation for TooComplex designs

M2's tests change: T-PHY-08 and the cleaned-parts and no-guard cases now pin the kept-parts rule, and the vote and mirror cases call validationFrame (the mirror case was renamed 'the grip frame mirrors'). M2's fast generated-design corpora became t.slow with their names kept, as item 8 allows past 27 s
T-DIF-07 (a)'s fast case was narrowed to C10 and C11 at +0.3317 for --quick time. The slow case still covers all 20 F and C fixtures, and T-EDG-01 6 checks all 111 shifted copies' edges in --quick
The charge tests identify loops by name via debug.info(2, 'n'), as V1 did, so renaming a loop's local function fails them
I corrected fixer A's re-cut figure 0.0378 / 0.0196 to this tree's 0.0379 / 0.0195 in the SPEC, E-S2.13, Factors' header and Invariance's header. Fixer A's own M3-notes section is left as its record

For the lead: on this tree, L3's option (a) (Douglas–Peucker on the integer lattice) would now meet L3's own criterion: no §5.5 or E-S2.9 value moves, and C15's tie disappeared with the centred raster. It would also make every Y shift exact. O11 now lists it as a way out with its cost; the default is still 'accept'

V4 still counts every Grip part, so a hidden Grip part can still make a design invalid (BladeNotAboveGrip) or valid; the player sees it as an error. totalLength still counts every part; no stat reads it
